_comment: Series config for the human psychology / power / influence flow. Read by scripts/generate_script_niche.py; the 'video' block is also passed to assemble_video.py --config. Add/remove topics freely.
channel_description: short human-psychology videos about power, influence, self-control and emotional mastery, grounded in well-established psychology
tone: calm, confident, second-person, thought-provoking; opens with a question or a surprising truth and ends on one memorable line
footage_hint: filmable stock scenes: chess pieces, a calm person in a busy crowd, a silhouette on a mountain, a lion or eagle, a person breathing deeply, a boardroom, city timelapse, storm clouds clearing, a person walking away, hands closing a book

examples.topic: Why the calmest person in the room holds the power
examples.title: WHO IS ACTUALLY WINNING THE ARGUMENT?
examples.narration: Two people in a meeting. One is shouting. One says nothing. Guess who's winning. Not the loud one. Every time he raises his voice, he tells the room one thing: I'm losing control. The quiet one is doing the opposite. She's giving everyone nothing to push against. And people read calm as confidence, even when it's just a pause. Power isn't volume. It's the gap between what happens and how you react. Close that gap, and the whole room starts waiting for you. Be the pause.

examples.topic: Why reacting gives your power away
examples.title: THEY INSULTED YOU ON PURPOSE
examples.narration: Someone insults you. You snap back. And just like that, you lost. Here's the part nobody tells you. That insult was a test. They wanted to see if a few words could move you. When you react, you prove they can. Now they know exactly which button to press, and they'll press it again. But wait three seconds. Breathe. Say nothing. Now the insult has nowhere to land. Try it once. Watch their face. Whoever controls your reaction controls you. So take it back.
